# Setup

```{r}
options(conflicts.policy = "depends.ok")
library(tidyverse)
plot_grid <- cowplot::plot_grid
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/format_path.R?raw=true")
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/fun_eda.R?raw=true")
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/fun_plots.R?raw=true")
source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/study_llmpanel/blob/main/scripts/functions_llmpanel.R?raw=true")
library(tidymodels)

path_processed <- format_path("llmpanel/data_processed")

# Read in full panel
panel <- read_csv(here::here(path_processed, "panel.csv"),
                       show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# Constant Demographic Features

The following features will be used in all recipes, without changes across model configurations:

## Sex

Sex at birth will be used as a dummy coded, dichotomous predictor: female (0.5) or male (-0.5).

```{r}
panel |> count(dem_sex)

panel <- panel |> 
  mutate(dem_sex = if_else(dem_sex == "female", 0.5, -0.5))

panel |> count(dem_sex)
```

## Orientation

Sexual Orientation will be used with collapsed categories Straight/Other, resulting from a lack of variability for non-straight orientations within the sample. 

```{r}
panel |> count(dem_orientation)

panel <- panel |> 
  mutate(dem_orientation = if_else(dem_orientation == "straight", "straight", "other"))
       
panel |> count(dem_orientation)
```

## Race / Ethnicity

Race will be used with collapsed categories White Only/Other, resulting from a lack of variability for non-white ethnicity groups within the sample.

```{r}
panel <- panel |>
  mutate(
    white = !is.na(dem_race_white),
    other =
      !is.na(dem_race_native_alaskan) |
      !is.na(dem_race_asian) |
      !is.na(dem_race_hispanic) |
      !is.na(dem_race_black),
    dem_race = if_else(white & !other, -0.5, +0.5))

panel |> count(dem_race)
```

## Household Size

Household size will be used in its raw numeric form (`dem_n_household`).

```{r}
panel |> count(dem_n_household)
```

# Adjustable Demographic Features

## Age

Age can be used in its raw numeric predictor form, or it can be binned into roughly equal categories:

```{r}
panel <- panel |>
  mutate(dem_age_binned = cut(
    dem_age, breaks = c(18, 29, 39, 49, 59, Inf),
    labels = c("18-29", "30-39", "40-49", "50-59", "60+"),
    right = TRUE, include.lowest = TRUE))

panel |> count(dem_age_binned)
```

The binned age predictor can be treated as either an ordinal or just a multi-category variable.

## Education

Education will be handled in two possible ways: The first option will be to treat it as an ordinal predictor with increasing amounts of education, and other will be to collapse into 3 categories.

```{r}
panel <- panel |>
  mutate(dem_edu_collapsed = case_when(
    dem_education %in% c("high_school_or_ged", "less_than_high_school_or_ged_degree") ~ "High School or Less",
    dem_education == "some_college" ~ "Some College",
    dem_education %in% c("2_year_degree", "4_year_degree", "advanced_degree") ~ "2-Year Degree or Higher"
  ))

panel |> count(dem_edu_collapsed)
```

## Income (+ Household Adjusted)

Income will be handled in 3 possible ways: First will be to treat income bracket as either a multi-category or ordinal variable.

Another engineered feature will be 'Household Size-Adjusted Income':

```{r}
panel <- panel |>
  mutate(
    income_numeric = case_when(
      dem_income == "Less than $25,000"   ~ 12500, # Midpoint estimates for each bracket
      dem_income == "$25,000 - $37,499"   ~ 31250,
      dem_income == "$37,500 - $49,999"   ~ 43750,
      dem_income == "$50,000 - $74,999"   ~ 62500,
      dem_income == "$75,000 - $99,999"   ~ 87500,
      dem_income == "$100,000 - $149,999" ~ 125000,
      dem_income == "$150,000 - $199,999" ~ 175000,
      dem_income == "$200,000 or more"    ~ 250000 # The cap for this one is debatable
    ),
    dem_income_adjusted = income_numeric / sqrt(dem_n_household))
```

There is precedent for this feature, and logically it is used to reflect 'economies of scale' in a household environment. The cost of living when moving from a 1 -> 2 person household will be greater than moving from a 5 -> 6 person household is the primary assumption that justifies the transformation of household size. The most tenuous assumption of this feature is choosing a numeric estimate for our highest income bracket, which did not have a fixed cap.

Household size is a constant feature, so it is included in every recipe. When this feature is included in a recipe, it may or may not have a separate predictor for income bracket included. As in, this feature could be used in addition to income bracket, or as a replacement for it to reduce dimensionality.

## Interactions

When explicitly defining interactions is required, the following combinations will be considered:

- Age x Income x Education

- Sex x Race x Orientation

- Age x Household Size

- Income x Household Size

# Pivot Long Format

The pivot happens after all demographic features are engineered so they carry through to the message-level data. Note that the feature engineering chunks above modify `panel` in place and are not idempotent (e.g., re-running the sex recode sets everyone to -0.5), so re-run from the Setup chunk if needed.

```{r}
panel_long <- panel |>
  select(subid, dem_age:dem_minority,
         dem_race, dem_age_binned, dem_edu_collapsed,
         dem_income_adjusted,
         q1_legitimizing_1:q6_formality_1,
         `x1_hi_1_fl_1`:`x4_li_10_in_1`,
         -contains("timing"), -contains("attention")) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols= `x1_hi_1_fl_1`:`x4_li_10_in_1`,
    values_to = "message_rating",
    names_to = "message_type") |>
  separate(message_type,
           sep = "_", into = c(
             "survey_version", "context", "q_num", "tone_style"),
           extra = "drop") |> 
  mutate(
    style = if_else(substr(tone_style, 1, 1) == "f", "formal", "informal"),
    tone = case_when(
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "l" ~ "legitimizing",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "n" ~ "norms",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "s" ~ "self_efficacy",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "a" ~ "acknowledging",
      substr(tone_style, 2, 2) == "v" ~ "value_affirmation"),
    context = case_when(
      context == "hi" ~ "high_increasing",
      context == "hd" ~ "high_decreasing",
      context == "li" ~ "low_increasing")
  ) |>
  select(-q_num, -tone_style) |> 
  filter(!is.na(message_rating),
         str_trim(message_rating) != "")

# Sanity-check that we have 30 rows per respondent
nrow(panel) * 30 == nrow(panel_long)
```

# GLMnet Recipes

GLMnet requires a fully numeric, complete design matrix, and the penalty assumes all predictors are on the same scale. Every recipe below therefore follows the same rules:

- **Outcome:** `message_rating` is scored 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree) and modeled as numeric (gaussian GLMnet).
- **Controls (all recipes):** attitude items `q1`–`q6` as ordinal scores, and `context`, `style`, `tone`, `survey_version` dummy coded.
- **Constant demographics (all recipes):** `dem_sex` (±0.5), `dem_race` (±0.5), `dem_orientation` (dummy coded), `dem_n_household` (raw numeric).
- **Nominal features** are dummy coded with `step_dummy()` (ordered factors are first converted with `step_unorder()` so they get treatment rather than polynomial contrasts). **Ordinal features** are converted to integer scores with `step_ordinalscore()`.
- **Interactions** are built after dummy coding and before normalization. Three-way terms include their two-way terms (`(a + b + c)^3`). When adjusted income is *added*, interactions use the income bracket. When it *replaces* income bracket, Age x Income x Education uses adjusted income, and Income x Household Size is dropped because adjusted income is already a function of household size.
- In the interaction variants, `step_nzv()` removes near-zero variance interaction columns (those containing `_x_`) using the default cutoffs (ratio of most-common to second-most-common value > 95/5 and < 10% unique values). It is limited to interaction columns so that main-effect dummies for small categories are kept. `step_zv()` then removes any remaining constant columns, and `step_normalize()` scales all predictors.

Configurations are the full crossing of:

| Feature | Options |
|---|---|
| Age | Numeric (`agenum`), Binned Nominal (`agenom`), Binned Ordinal (`ageord`) |
| Education | Ordinal (`eduord`), Collapsed Nominal (`edunom`) |
| Income | Nominal (`incnom`), Ordinal (`incord`) |
| Adjusted Income | Absent, Added to income bracket (`_adj`), Replaces income bracket (`adjinc`) |

This gives 3 x 2 x (2 x 2 + 1) = 30 main-effect configurations, each with an all-interactions variant (suffix `_int`), for 60 recipes. Feature sets are baked and summarized but not stored, to keep memory manageable.

Demographics are constant within respondent, so the effective sample size for demographic effects is the number of respondents (n = 424), not the number of ratings. The interaction variants with several nominal features produce many sparse columns before `step_nzv()`, and penalization will be doing much of the work there.

## GLMnet Setup

```{r}
rating_levels <- c("strongly_disagree", "disagree", "somewhat_disagree", "neutral",
                   "somewhat_agree", "agree", "strongly_agree")
formality_levels <- c("strongly_prefer_formal", "moderately_prefer_formal", "slightly_prefer_formal",
                      "slightly_prefer_informal", "moderately_prefer_informal", "strongly_prefer_informal")
education_levels <- c("less_than_high_school_or_ged_degree", "high_school_or_ged", "some_college",
                      "2_year_degree", "4_year_degree", "advanced_degree")
income_levels <- c("Less than $25,000", "$25,000 - $37,499", "$37,500 - $49,999", "$50,000 - $74,999",
                   "$75,000 - $99,999", "$100,000 - $149,999", "$150,000 - $199,999", "$200,000 or more")

# Short labels give readable dummy column names
d_glmnet <- panel_long |>
  mutate(
    message_rating = as.numeric(factor(message_rating, levels = rating_levels)),
    across(q1_legitimizing_1:q5_norms_1,
           \(x) factor(x, levels = rating_levels, ordered = TRUE)),
    q6_formality_1 = factor(q6_formality_1, levels = formality_levels, ordered = TRUE),
    dem_age_binned = factor(dem_age_binned,
      labels = c("under_30", "age_30s", "age_40s", "age_50s", "age_60_plus"),
      ordered = TRUE),
    dem_education = factor(dem_education, levels = education_levels, ordered = TRUE),
    dem_edu_collapsed = factor(dem_edu_collapsed,
      levels = c("High School or Less", "Some College", "2-Year Degree or Higher"),
      labels = c("hs_or_less", "some_college", "degree_2yr_plus")),
    dem_income = factor(dem_income, levels = income_levels,
      labels = c("under_25k", "from_25k", "from_37k", "from_50k",
                 "from_75k", "from_100k", "from_150k", "from_200k"),
      ordered = TRUE),
    across(c(context, style, tone, survey_version, dem_orientation), factor))

glmnet_controls <- c("q1_legitimizing_1", "q2_self_efficacy_1", "q3_acknowledging_1",
                     "q4_value_affirmation_1", "q5_norms_1", "q6_formality_1",
                     "context", "style", "tone", "survey_version")
glmnet_dem_constant <- c("dem_sex", "dem_race", "dem_orientation", "dem_n_household")

d_glmnet |>
  select(message_rating, all_of(glmnet_controls), all_of(glmnet_dem_constant),
         dem_age, dem_age_binned, dem_education, dem_edu_collapsed,
         dem_income, dem_income_adjusted) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0)
```

Shared recipe start (outcome, ID, controls, constant demographics) and a feature set review helper:

```{r}
rec_glmnet_base <- function(dem_adjustable, data = d_glmnet) {
  rec_formula <- reformulate(
    c("subid", glmnet_controls, glmnet_dem_constant, dem_adjustable),
    response = "message_rating")

  recipe(rec_formula, data = data) |>
    update_role(subid, new_role = "id") |>
    step_ordinalscore(matches("^q[1-6]_")) |>
    step_dummy(context, style, tone, survey_version, dem_orientation)
}

review_features <- function(feat) {
  predictors <- setdiff(names(feat), c("subid", "message_rating"))
  dem <- str_subset(predictors, "^dem_")
  tibble(
    n_obs = nrow(feat),
    n_predictors = length(predictors),
    n_dem_main = sum(!str_detect(dem, "_x_")),
    n_dem_interactions = sum(str_detect(dem, "_x_")),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(feat))
  ) |>
    print()
  feat |>
    select(all_of(dem), -contains("_x_")) |>
    glimpse()
}
```

## Age: Numeric | Education: Ordinal

### Income: Nominal

#### Main Effects

```{r}
rec_glmnet_agenum_eduord_incnom <- rec_glmnet_base(
  c("dem_age", "dem_education", "dem_income")) |>
  step_unorder(dem_income) |>
  step_ordinalscore(dem_education) |>
  step_dummy(dem_income) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_predictors())

rec_glmnet_agenum_eduord_incnom |>
  prep() |>
  bake(new_data = NULL) |>
  review_features()
```

#### All Interactions

```{r}
rec_glmnet_agenum_eduord_incnom_int <- rec_glmnet_base(
  c("dem_age", "dem_education", "dem_income")) |>
  step_unorder(dem_income) |>
  step_ordinalscore(dem_education) |>
  step_dummy(dem_income) |>
  step_interact(terms = ~ (dem_age + starts_with("dem_income_") + dem_education)^3) |>
  step_interact(terms = ~ (dem_sex + dem_race + starts_with("dem_orientation_"))^3) |>
  step_interact(terms = ~ dem_age:dem_n_household) |>
  step_interact(terms = ~ starts_with("dem_income_"):dem_n_household) |>
  step_nzv(contains("_x_")) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_predictors())

rec_glmnet_agenum_eduord_incnom_int |>
  prep() |>
  bake(new_data = NULL) |>
  review_features()
```

## Rebuilding Recipes from Configuration Codes

`rec_glmnet_build()` rebuilds any of the 60 recipes above from its configuration code (the recipe object name without the `rec_glmnet_` prefix, e.g. `"agenom_edunom_incnom_adj_int"`). It applies the same encoding and interaction rules as the hand-written recipes, so downstream scripts can loop over `glmnet_configs$config` instead of copying recipe code. It depends on `d_glmnet`, `glmnet_controls`, `glmnet_dem_constant`, and `rec_glmnet_base()` from the GLMnet Setup section.

```{r}
# One row per configuration code: the variable it uses, how it is encoded,
# and the term it contributes to step_interact()
glmnet_feature_specs <- tribble(
  ~code,    ~var,                  ~encoding,         ~int_term,
  "agenum", "dem_age",             "numeric",         "dem_age",
  "agenom", "dem_age_binned",      "nominal_ordered", 'starts_with("dem_age_binned_")',
  "ageord", "dem_age_binned",      "ordinal",         "dem_age_binned",
  "eduord", "dem_education",       "ordinal",         "dem_education",
  "edunom", "dem_edu_collapsed",   "nominal",         'starts_with("dem_edu_collapsed_")',
  "incnom", "dem_income",          "nominal_ordered", 'starts_with("dem_income_")',
  "incord", "dem_income",          "ordinal",         "dem_income",
  "adj",    "dem_income_adjusted", "numeric",         NA,
  "adjinc", "dem_income_adjusted", "numeric",         "dem_income_adjusted"
)

glmnet_configs <- expand_grid(
  age = c("agenum", "agenom", "ageord"),
  edu = c("eduord", "edunom"),
  inc = c("incnom", "incnom_adj", "incord", "incord_adj", "adjinc"),
  int = c("", "_int")) |>
  mutate(config = str_c(age, "_", edu, "_", inc, int))

rec_glmnet_build <- function(config, data = d_glmnet) {
  if (length(config) != 1 || !config %in% glmnet_configs$config) {
    stop("Unknown GLMnet configuration: '", paste(config, collapse = ", "),
         "'. See `glmnet_configs$config` for valid codes.")
  }

  parts <- str_split_1(config, "_")
  specs <- glmnet_feature_specs[match(setdiff(parts, "int"), glmnet_feature_specs$code), ]
  vars_with <- \(enc) specs$var[specs$encoding %in% enc]

  rec <- rec_glmnet_base(specs$var, data = data)
  if (length(vars_with("nominal_ordered")) > 0) {
    rec <- rec |> step_unorder(all_of(vars_with("nominal_ordered")))
  }
  if (length(vars_with("ordinal")) > 0) {
    rec <- rec |> step_ordinalscore(all_of(vars_with("ordinal")))
  }
  if (length(vars_with(c("nominal", "nominal_ordered"))) > 0) {
    rec <- rec |> step_dummy(all_of(vars_with(c("nominal", "nominal_ordered"))))
  }

  if ("int" %in% parts) {
    term_for <- \(prefix) specs$int_term[str_starts(specs$code, prefix)]
    adj_only <- "adjinc" %in% parts
    age_term <- term_for("age")
    edu_term <- term_for("edu")
    inc_term <- if (adj_only) term_for("adjinc") else term_for("inc")
    # Keep dem_income_adjusted out of the income-bracket dummy selector
    if (all(c("adj", "incnom") %in% parts)) {
      inc_term <- 'matches("^dem_income_(?!adjusted)", perl = TRUE)'
    }

    int_formulas <- c(
      paste0("~ (", age_term, " + ", inc_term, " + ", edu_term, ")^3"),
      '~ (dem_sex + dem_race + starts_with("dem_orientation_"))^3',
      paste0("~ ", age_term, ":dem_n_household"))
    # Adjusted income already incorporates household size
    if (!adj_only) {
      int_formulas <- c(int_formulas, paste0("~ ", inc_term, ":dem_n_household"))
    }
    for (f in int_formulas) {
      rec <- rec |> step_interact(terms = !!as.formula(f))
    }
    rec <- rec |> step_nzv(contains("_x_"))
  }

  rec |>
    step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
    step_normalize(all_predictors())
}

glmnet_configs |> count(int)
```

Example usage:

```{r}
rec_glmnet_build("agenom_edunom_incnom_adj_int") |>
  prep() |>
  bake(new_data = NULL) |>
  review_features()
```

Check that the builder matches the hand-written recipes for a spread of configurations (every encoding option, each adjusted-income option, with and without interactions):

```{r}
check_configs <- c("agenum_eduord_incnom", "agenom_edunom_incnom_adj_int",
                   "ageord_eduord_incord_int", "agenom_eduord_incnom_adj",
                   "ageord_edunom_adjinc_int", "agenum_edunom_adjinc")

map_lgl(check_configs, \(cfg) {
  hand <- get(str_c("rec_glmnet_", cfg)) |> prep() |> bake(new_data = NULL)
  built <- rec_glmnet_build(cfg) |> prep() |> bake(new_data = NULL)
  identical(hand, built)
}) |>
  set_names(check_configs)
```
